decisions.diagnosis: A weekend closure of the cycleway, not a counter outage: both directions carry small scattered counts all day, so the partial zero_outage flags remove real low counts.
decisions.evidence: Raw East 76/30 and West 50/25 on Sat/Sun against typical weekend levels of about 190; hourly counts are 0-10 spread through the day in both directions, and part of the weekend is flagged while the rest is kept.

decisions.diagnosis: Repeated weekend closures (Friday about 21:30 to Monday about 05:30) plus one full closure from 2017-07-01 to 2017-07-09: real near-zero riding that zero_outage set to missing.
decisions.evidence: 13 separate Fri-night-to-Mon-morning windows with raw 0-29 per day in both directions (for example East on 2017-03-25/26 had 2/1). The zeros start and end at the same clock times each time, and one direction was sometimes flagged while the other was kept (2017-03-18 West 23 kept, East 7 flagged). A counter fault would not follow the works calendar like this.

decisions.diagnosis: The same Friday-night-to-Monday-morning closure pattern (2018-08-24, 08-31, 09-21, 12-14, 2019-02-08, 02-22, 03-22), plus overnight zeros wrongly flagged on 2018-07-01: real low counts, not outages.
decisions.evidence: On closure weekends the unflagged direction is also depressed (West 2018-08-25/26 at 92/55 against a median of about 290/250). Flagged days hold scattered raw counts of 0-48, and only zero_outage fixes occur in this span.

decisions.diagnosis: A sensor fault: from 09:15 to 14:15 West has a single channel reporting a steady 25-69 per slot while East reads 0, which doubles the West day total.
decisions.evidence: West 1180 against 537 the next day and a weekday median of about 598. In slots 37-57 exactly one of the four channels is non-zero, totalling about 750 bikes over 19 slots; East is all zeros in the same window. No other day in 2016-2025 has this pattern.

decisions.diagnosis: The counter failed in the evening of 2023-12-07 and gave degraded, partly duplicated West counts on 2023-12-08, leading into the outage of 12-09 to 12-15.
decisions.evidence: Both directions fall after 18:00 on 12-07 (West 43/17 per hour against 116/115 the day before). On 12-08 East raw is 62 and West clean is 344 (from raw 688 at 5.5 records per slot) with no morning peak, while neighbours 545 and 551 were normal (551 East 660).

decisions.diagnosis: The sensor degraded progressively in both directions before the warning outage of 2024-03-11 to 2024-03-16, while nearby counters were normal.
decisions.evidence: Weekday East fell 459, 371, 250, 118 and West 746, 678, 473, 348 (normally about 1200 each). Over the same days 551 East read 759-897 and 542 read 1012-1165, both normal. On 03-03 the Sunday ratio to 551 was 1.1 against 2.1 the week before. Counts were back to 1039/1160 on 03-18.

series.name: Old counter, AM-peak flow (labelled East)
series.evidence: Ecocounter 228, 2016-05 to 2024-08, with a morning peak at 08:00. New counter 357 (from 2025-10, after a 14-month gap) reads about 55% higher (about 1450/day against 940) with a flatter daily and weekly profile, while neighbouring sites rose only about 30-35% at their own replacements, so comparability cannot be established.

series.name: Old counter, PM-peak flow (labelled West)
series.evidence: Ecocounter 228 West, with an evening peak at 17:00. Kept separate from 357/1751 (the same flow by profile) because of the gap and a level step of about 57% that cannot be verified.

series.name: New counter, AM-peak flow (labelled West)
series.evidence: Metrocount 357. Its 'West' direction has the morning peak (205 at 08:00), so it carries the same flow as old 340 'East': the East/West labels are swapped between the counters, while the citybound flags agree. It is kept separate because the level is not comparable.

series.name: New counter, PM-peak flow (labelled East)
series.evidence: Metrocount 357 'East', with an evening peak (240 at 17:00), is the same flow as old 341 'West'. It is kept separate because the level is not comparable.

summary: Liverpool St at Kent St was counted by a 4-channel Ecocounter from 2016 to 2024 and by a Metrocount from October 2025; the new counter reads about 55% higher with a flatter profile and swapped East/West labels, so the four counter-directions are separate series. In 2016-2019 zero_outage removed recurring Friday-night-to-Monday-morning cycleway closures, which I restore as real low counts. Three short fault periods (a phantom single-channel burst on 2021-08-04, failure days in December 2023 and a degrading sensor in March 2024) are set missing; the duplicate-record fixes and the long outages (2021-02, 2023-03 to 2023-08, 2024-08 to 2025-06) are correct as applied.
